newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gotthard Bank buys Geneva private bank.
newsitem.headline: Gotthard Bank buys Geneva private bank.

text.p: Gotthard Bank said it bought a 75 percent stake in Banque de Gestion Privee, the fourth takeover so far this year in Geneva's private banking market which is struggling with tough competition.
Banque de Gestion Privee will be incorporated into the Lugano-based bank's Geneva operation, the head of Gotthard Bank's Geneva branch, Giuliano Castelli, told Reuters.
"This is a requirement of the market and changes in the banking industry," he said. "The acquisition will help us develop our business."

Gotthard Bank, owned 55 percent by Japan's Sumitomo Bank Ltd, did not disclose how much it paid for the shares of Banque de Gestion Privee, which has some 400 million Swiss francs in client assets under management.
Bankers say the private banking business is a cash cow, contributing to more than half of profits at the big three Swiss banks.
The top three Swiss banks, Union Bank of Switzerland Credit Suisse and Swiss Bank Corporation, make no secret of their acquisition plans to fuel growth in private banking business.

Swiss Bank Corporation said last week that it was buying Dillon, Read & Co Inc, one of the best-managed U.S. investment banks, for about $600 million stock and combining it with its SBC Warburg investment bank.

In 1996, Dillon Read was an adviser on 50 mergers and acquisitions deals with an aggregate value of $45 billion and its deals in high yield, equity offerings and private placements totaled $8 billion last year.
Private bankers expect acquisitions to pick up in Geneva, where the arrival of such Wall Street powerhouses as Merrill Lynch has disrupted the once cosy world of old, established Swiss private banks.

In February, a Malaysian conglomerate, George Town Holdings Bhd, said it was acquiring the Geneva private bank Banque Financiere de la Cite SA (BFC) and its offshore operation based in the Cayman islands for 45 million Swiss francs.

Also in February, Geneva private banks Banque D'Investissements Prives (BIP) and Compagnie Bancaire Geneve (CBG) announced a merger plan to join forces against competition in a deal put at more than 50 million Swiss francs by bankers.

That followed another Geneva sale by U.S. brokerage house Lehman Brothers of its fully-owned Swiss private bank to Vancouver-based Canadian asset management and financial services group MFC Financial Corp for an undisclosed sum.
